title: Axeyum Obstruction Graph
description: A DERIVED, overlay-shaped sidecar turning typed declines into obstruction clusters (Autogenesis F3, docs/autogenesis/243-knowledge-overlay-and-fill-plan.md; slice A5 of docs/python-2026-08/03-agentic-layer.md). Three properties are load-bearing. (1) It is GENERATED, never hand-authored: scripts/gen-obstruction-graph.py derives every entity and link from committed agent episodes and committed producer decline records, and `--check` fails when the committed file differs from a regeneration. Doc 243's rule is that this graph must be derivable rather than authored, and a hand-edited row would be a claim nobody measured. (2) It is a SIDECAR and never an edit to artifacts/autogenesis/knowledge-overlay-v1.json. The overlay already declares `obstruction` as an entity kind and `blocked-by` as a relation, and this document mirrors the overlay's link shape field for field so the two can be read together -- but it declares its own namespaces and its own endpoint kinds, because `tactic` is NOT an overlay entity kind and pretending otherwise would let a sidecar row be merged verbatim into a document whose schema forbids it. (3) Its assurance ceiling is `mechanically-observed`. Every row here is an observation about what a run did, not a mathematical claim: nothing in it is kernel-derived, checker-derived, registry-derived, or human-reviewed, and the enum below cannot express those values at all. An obstruction is evidence that a route did not close a goal; it is never evidence that the goal is false, and never evidence that any capability named in `candidate_capability` would in fact close it.

generated_by.description: The generator that owns this file. A reader who wants to change a row edits the generator or the evidence, never this document.

inputs.description: Every file the derivation read, with the digest it read. This is what makes a regeneration comparable: a changed input changes a digest here before it changes any count.

entities.description: The obstruction clusters. Empty is not a valid graph: a derivation that found nothing is a derivation that was pointed at nothing, and the generator exits 1 rather than committing an empty census.

assurance.description: The CEILING is `mechanically-observed` and the enum enforces it: the overlay's `formal-derived`, `independently-checked`, `registry-derived` and `human-reviewed` are deliberately absent, so no row in this file can claim a kernel, a checker, a registry or a person stood behind it. An obstruction is a thing a run did, observed from committed bytes.

status.description: `open`: the cluster still blocks its population. `mitigated`: a capability landed and the funnel moved but the cluster is not empty. `resolved`: the population is no longer blocked, and `resolution.commit` names the change that did it.

declineClass.description: The v2 episode enum, verbatim from artifacts/ontology/agent-episode-v2.schema.json, plus `null` for evidence that is not an episode (a producer decline record predates the loop and carries no episode decline class). The nine AG4.1 classes and the five loop-local ones are NOT merged here for the same reason the episode schema keeps them apart: `no-general-route` is a result the model produced, not a mathematical obstruction anyone observed.

blockerKind.description: Derived from the evidence that exists, not invented. Each value is produced by a structural predicate over a committed document, and each was observed at least once when this enum was written (2026-08-24). `no-general-route`, `export-missing`, `budget` and `gate-refused` come from the 16 committed episodes; `axiom-footprint-nonempty`, `elaboration-blocked`, `tooling-gate-refused`, `tactic-precondition-unmatched` and `replay-readiness-mismatch` come from the 11 committed producer decline records. A record whose shape matches none of them is classified `unclassified`, and the generator EXITS 1 on that -- a new decline shape that silently vanished from the census would be the checker-that-cannot-fail defect one arrow upstream.

endpointKind.description: `fact`, `capability`, `operation` and `obstruction` are overlay entity kinds and mean exactly what the overlay means by them. `tactic` is NOT: the overlay has no tactic kind, and a `T:` id resolves in artifacts/autogenesis/tactic-catalog-v1.json. It is kept as its own kind rather than filed under the overlay's `producer` or `technique` so that nobody can copy a link from this file into the overlay and have it validate.

funnel.description: F3's normalization, counted over the committed episodes: goal -> adapter -> producer -> reconstruction -> checker -> obstruction. Every stage is a predicate over one episode document and nothing else. `adapter` counts a tier-C dispatch whose frozen statement export RESOLVED, so a dispatch that came back `retrieval-miss` is counted at `goal` and not at `adapter` -- which is the point: it is where the population is actually lost. `checker` is the registry/transaction stage (prepare-autogenesis-fact-transaction.py exiting 0), NOT the independent kernel re-check, which is `reconstruction`. Those two are different findings and collapsing them would hide that a fact can be kernel-proved and still have nowhere to land.

blocker.description: One observed blocker. `kind` is the taxonomy value a predicate produced; `detail` is the finer discriminator the evidence carried verbatim (a tactic id, an axiom name, the elaborator operation that was refused); `observed_in` is the file it came from. The CLUSTER key uses `kind` plus the COARSE detail; `known_blockers` keeps every distinct fine-grained pair, which is how `first observed blocker` and `complete known blocker set` stay separate rather than one overwriting the other.

source.description: Which typed field the predicate read. A blocker derived from a proposal variant is a different quality of evidence from one derived from a producer's own Rust enum variant, and the distinction is not recoverable from `kind`.

population.description: Who this obstruction blocks. `partitions` counts by nursery partition and MUST NOT contain `held-out`: the generator and the validator both refuse the document when it does, and neither treats an absent key as a pass. A capsule registered against one held-out row cost 19 of 76 held-out propositions on 2026-08-21; a census that merely enumerated one would be the same class of spend.

candidateCapability.description: The capability that would remove this cluster, and whether it already exists. `exists` is measured against artifacts/autogenesis/knowledge-overlay-v1.json, not asserted: an id outside that file must be spelled `K:proposed-...` so a reader cannot mistake a wish for an entity. `exists: true` is the interesting case and it is not the flattering one -- it says the capability is already built and has not been pointed at the cluster, which is a scheduling finding rather than an engineering one.

resolution.description: `commit` is null until something removes the cluster. `before` is the funnel measured over this cluster's own episode evidence NOW; `after` stays null until a resolution commit exists and the same population is re-run, because a before/after that was never measured twice is not a before/after.

evidence.description: A committed file and the digest it had when this row was derived. `sha256` is re-hashed from disk by the validator; a mismatch is an error, not a warning, because an obstruction that cites bytes nobody can reproduce is prose.

cluster_key.description: The exact string the id is derived from: `<first blocker kind>|<coarse detail>`. Printed so a reader can re-derive the id by hand with sha256 and see that nothing was assigned by judgement.

decline_classes.description: Every distinct v2 decline class the cluster's episode evidence carried. More than one is normal and informative: the same obstruction recorded `no-general-route` under the A2 graph and `gate-refused` under A4, because A4 added a gate that refuses a NoGeneralRoute plan. The obstruction did not change; the harness did.

link.description: Field for field the overlay's link shape (id / relation / source / target / assurance / status / reason / provenance / evidence), so the two documents read together. `blocked-by` points from a fact, a tactic or a capability TO the obstruction, matching the overlay's own `blocked-by` direction.
